Research suggests that fertility is influenced by several factors, including age, overall health, lifestyle habits, and certain medical conditions. While fertility concerns are often associated with women, studies have shown that male factors can also play an important role.

Some commonly misunderstood facts include:
• Fertility can change with age
• Lifestyle habits may affect reproductive health
• Regular periods do not always reflect fertility status
• Fertility concerns can affect both partners

Understanding these factors early can help people make informed decisions and seek timely evaluation when needed. Greater awareness may also help avoid delays in identifying concerns that could affect future pregnancy planning.

A few important awareness points:
• Maintain a healthy lifestyle
• Avoid smoking and excessive alcohol consumption
• Do not ignore changes in menstrual health

Menstrual cycles often begin to change after the age of 40.

Changes that may require evaluation include:

• Bleeding between periods
• Very heavy menstrual flow
• Periods that become unusually frequent
• Bleeding that lasts longer than usual
• Bleeding after menopause
• Severe pelvic pain or unusual discharge

The proposed shift toward PMOS reflects this broader understanding and the importance of looking at hormonal health more comprehensively rather than limiting the conversation only to reproductive symptoms.

PELVIC FLOOR EXCERCISE-
Pelvic floor exercises (Kegels) strengthen the muscles that support your bladder and bowels. To locate the muscles, imagine stopping the flow of urine or trying to prevent passing gas. Squeeze and lift these muscles for 3-5 seconds, then relax completely for 3-5 seconds. Repeat 10-15 times per session, doing 3 sets daily.

How to do them right Follow these steps to ensure you are targeting the right muscles without straining:
Empty your bladder: Always start with an empty bladder to prevent discomfort.
Find the muscles: Squeeze the muscles that stop the flow of urine or hold back gas. You should feel a lifting sensation inside.
The Squeeze: Tighten these muscles and hold for 3 to 5 seconds.
The Relaxation: Relax completely for 3 to 5 seconds.
Set and Repetition: Repeat this 10 to 15 times in a row to complete one session.
Frequency: Do this 3 times a day (morning, afternoon, and 
night).

DYSMENORRHOEA
causes severe and frequent cramps and pain during your period. It may be either primary or secondary.

Primary dysmenorrhea. This occurs when you first start your period and continues throughout your life. It is usually life-long. It can cause severe and frequent menstrual cramping from severe and abnormal uterine contractions.

Secondary dysmenorrhea. This type is due to some physical cause. It usually starts later in life. It may be caused by another medical condition, such as pelvic inflammatory disease or endometriosis.

MENORRHAGIA ( HEAVY BLEEDING DURING MENSE )

Menorrhagia is defined as abnormally heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding (typically lasting >7–8 days or passing large clots) that disrupts daily life also weakness, fainting, anemia .
 Common causes include hormonal imbalances, uterine fibroids, or any other uterine pathologies.
